messages.content: I confirmed the client will not cover Friday night, so use the Tuesday evening arrival and Friday evening return. I need a hotel for June 9 through June 12 near the downtown Denver workshop. The room has to stay at or below $225 a night before tax.
That makes it a three-night stay, checking in Tuesday and out Friday. What is the workshop address, and should I optimize mainly for the 8:00 a.m. start or for the lowest total within the cap?
It's at 1700 Broadway. Please compare both. I don't want a cheap room that turns the morning into a hassle, but cancellation matters while the flight is still only being held.

I found three workable refundable rates. The closest is the Grand Hyatt Denver at $219 per night, about a 7-minute walk. Its room total is $657 before tax, estimated at $755 after tax, but free cancellation ends at 6:00 p.m. on June 6. The Hampton Inn & Suites Downtown is $184 per night, about a 15-minute walk or 5–8 minutes by rideshare; total is $552 before tax and about $634 after tax, with cancellation until 11:59 p.m. on June 8. The Hilton Garden Inn Union Station is $169 per night, roughly 18–25 minutes by light rail and walking or 8–12 minutes by rideshare; total is $507 before tax and about $582 after tax, also cancellable through June 8.
Does the Grand Hyatt rate include anything useful, or is the extra cost basically just the location?

The quoted rate includes Wi-Fi and access to the fitness center, but breakfast is not included. Its practical advantage is the short walk: you could leave around 7:45 and still have a modest buffer. The Hampton includes breakfast and Wi-Fi. The Hilton Garden Inn includes Wi-Fi, while breakfast costs extra.
The Hampton sounds like the best value. Is that 15-minute walk realistic at that hour, or is it one of those estimates that ignores crossings?

The mapped route is about 0.7 mile and includes several downtown crossings, so I would budget 16–20 minutes in the morning. Leaving by 7:30 should put you at the venue before 7:50. A rideshare is short, but pickup and traffic could make its door-to-door time similar.
And no mandatory destination fee on that rate? Also compare the actual savings against the Hyatt after tax.

No destination or resort fee is listed for the Hampton rate. Its estimated after-tax total is $634 versus $755 at the Grand Hyatt, a savings of about $121 for the stay. It also gives you roughly two additional days to cancel and includes breakfast, in exchange for an extra 10–13 minutes of walking each morning.
What kind of room is available at $184? I only need one bed.
The $184 refundable option is a standard king room. A two-queen room is $196 per night, so there is no reason to move up unless you need the second bed.
Use the Hampton king as the hotel choice. Keep the Hyatt noted only as the close-in backup. Does the Hampton still fit if the taxes come in a little higher than estimated?

Yes. The reimbursement limit applies to the $184 pretax room rate, which is $41 below the $225 nightly cap. Even if the tax estimate shifts slightly, the qualifying room rate does not change. The current estimate is $552 before tax and approximately $634 after tax for all three nights.
Good. Pair that with the Friday-return flight and leave both unbooked. Give me the cancellation cutoff in local time and the morning plan to carry forward.

Carry forward the Hampton Inn & Suites Denver-Downtown standard king for June 9–12 at $184 per night: $552 before tax and about $634 after tax. Free cancellation runs through 11:59 p.m. Mountain Time on Monday, June 8; after that, the listed penalty is one night's room and tax. For the 8:00 a.m. workshop at 1700 Broadway, plan to leave on foot by 7:30 for a 16–20 minute walk. The Grand Hyatt remains the backup at $219 per night, about a 7-minute walk, with cancellation ending June 6 at 6:00 p.m. Mountain Time. Pair the Hampton with the $412 Tuesday-evening/Friday-evening nonstop itinerary. The flight and hotel are both still unbooked.
